clue.text: Fire in carousel

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the next word, tucked among its letters

parts.note: the letters run unbroken inside this word, minus its first and last

explanation.surface: A blaze breaks out on a fairground merry-go-round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' reads as a noun for a blaze, but it is the verb, as in firing someone's imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to stir or excite them, a verb synonym for rousing feeling.

clue.text: So be it about copper's shrewdness!

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the first phrase's word goes round the metal's symbol

parts.note: the word said at the end of a prayer, meaning 'so be it'
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a police officer's sharp judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal, standing for its chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is keen insight and good judgement, a direct synonym for shrewdness.

clue.text: Stubborn, set — obtain broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone fixed in their views insists on getting something put on air.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate person refuses to change their mind, which is exactly what stubborn means.

clue.text: Slight burn, just one, after learner's gone

indicators.note: something gone has left, so the learner's letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a single is just one of something
L is the learner plate sign

explanation.surface: A minor scorch, only one, once the novice has left the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGLE loses its L. L plates mark a learner driver in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn lightly at the surface or edges, a slight scorching.

clue.text: Insist two daughters retain name, after reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the whole result is read right to left
to retain is to hold on to, so the pair of letters keep the next word inside them

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter, taken twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: After some thought, a parent insists that both daughters keep the family surname.
explanation.walkthrough: D and D hold NAME to make DNAMED, which turned round gives DEMAND.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand is to call for something forcefully, the same as insisting on it.

clue.text: Time of day, flat, is no good principally

parts.note: a flat surface is even

indicators.note: principally means at the head, so only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: the initial letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A grumble that some hour of the day is dull and pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening is the part of the day between afternoon and night, so it names a time of day.

clue.text: Something done in Ascot regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the racecourse is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: Something that routinely happens at the races at Ascot.
explanation.walkthrough: Ascot is an English racecourse famous for its royal race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An act is a deed, a thing performed, so it is something done.

clue.text: Maybe tone down musical instrument after I'd flipped?

indicators.note: 'after' puts the instrument behind the other piece, so the contraction's letters come first
something flipped is turned over, so the short word is read backwards

parts.note: the contraction's letters
the lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A musician wondering whether they softened the tune once they lost their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' signals that toning down is just one example of diluting; 'after' places the instrument behind the turned letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute is to weaken or make less intense, of which toning down something is an example.

clue.text: Annulment site unusually hard-nosed?

indicators.note: unusually means in a way out of the ordinary, so these letters are set out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The venue for cancelling a marriage is oddly tough-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hard-nosed is tough and realistic, unswayed by feelings, which is being unsentimental.

clue.text: Cover in case run goes awry?

indicators.note: a plan that goes awry goes wrong and out of order, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Protection taken out against the chance that things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes what insurance is for, which makes the surface so convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance cover is the protection a policy provides, so cover is a common term for it.

clue.text: Best leaders of enterprise leaving in the end

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the front letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: The top people at a company end up departing.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best or most select members of a group, a noun sense of the best.

clue.text: Cutting second drink, much-liked

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a nip is a small measure of spirits
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone cuts themselves off a second drink of a favourite tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' is a noun here, a piece cut from a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting from a newspaper is a small extract, and a snippet is a small piece taken from something larger.

clue.text: One admitted to appalling missteps — I see trouble ahead

indicators.note: admitted to means let inside, so the single letter goes within the other letters
something appalling is dreadful and a mess, so these letters are rearranged badly

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone owns up to dreadful blunders and foresees more problems coming.
explanation.walkthrough: MISSTEPS rearranged gives PESSMIST, and I slips in to make PESSIMIST. The definition is the sort of thing such a person says.
explanation.definitionFit: A pessimist always expects the worst, so 'I see trouble ahead' is a fair description in their own words.

clue.text: Vegetable when of expected standard, first-class, ultimately pleasing us

parts.note: as in 'as he arrived', meaning when
par is the expected standard, as in golf
A is the top grade

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

parts.note: final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegetable that, when up to standard and top quality, ends up delighting us.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a green spring vegetable whose tender shoots are eaten.

clue.text: Herb, son, involved in wartime discussion perhaps

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be inside it, so the single letter goes within the talk

parts.note: a parley is a talk between enemies, typically during a war
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy named Herb takes part in some sort of wartime talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' reads as a man's name, but it is the plant. PARLEY holds S.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsley is a common leafy herb used in cooking and as a garnish.

clue.text: Element beginning to show hatred

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that letter is taken

parts.note: opening letter
odium is intense hatred or disgust

explanation.surface: A basic part of someone's behaviour starts to reveal loathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium is a chemical element, a soft reactive metal with symbol Na.

clue.text: Inadequately small, extremely minute — agree? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the word loses its final letter
extremely here means at the extremes, so the two end letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you agree that something is too tiny, then hedges.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means lacking in quantity or quality, scanty and too small to suffice.

clue.text: Extend beyond limit due to arguing at regular intervals

parts.note: as in a quarrel over money, meaning on account of it

indicators.note: at regular intervals means skipping evenly, so only every second letter is kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A meeting runs past its time because people keep quarrelling now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to go past an allotted time or boundary, so it means extending beyond a limit.

clue.text: Place of worship missing Queen's lustre

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the monarch's letter is taken away from the building

parts.note: a shrine is a holy place
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A holy site lacks the gleam the monarch once gave it.
explanation.walkthrough: SHRINE drops R; the 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a soft glow or gloss on a surface, which is a synonym for shine.

clue.text: Cheek dressing

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a liquid poured over food

explanation.walkthrough: The pair reads like a facial bandage, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal for impertinent talk and also a liquid served with food, like a salad dressing.

clue.text: The writer's beat, accepting shopping without much forethought

parts.note: the writer is I, and 'writer's' is 'I am', shortened
a pulse is a regular beat
to buy an argument is to accept it

explanation.surface: An author confesses to being worn out yet agreeing to go to the shops on a whim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' is a crossword way for the setter to say I.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse buy is a purchase made on a sudden whim, with no planning beforehand.

clue.text: For every person? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half is left, so the second half of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about sharing out to each individual, met by an emphatic answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is a British exclamation meaning 'very much so', which hides its job of cutting a word in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Per means for each, as in ten dollars per person, so it stands for 'for every'.

clue.text: Victim of railway vehicle reversing

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: RY is an abbreviation for railway
a tram is a vehicle on rails

explanation.surface: Someone hit by a train backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone who suffers or dies for a cause, a victim of persecution.

clue.text: Enclosed space containing protesters? It will reach boiling point!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a police cordon that hems demonstrators in
second meaning, cryptically: an appliance for heating water

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads like protesters' tempers rising, but it is the household appliance. Kettling is a police tactic of penning in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Police containment of a crowd is called a kettle, and a kettle is also the pot that brings water to the boil.
